look_here_first: FIRST CHECK THE LEAVES: E. angusta (narrowleaf spurge) is an ERECT, narrow-leaved perennial, not a creeping sandmat. Upper leaves are extremely narrow—typically more than six times longer than wide. Look for short white appressed (strigose) hairs on leaves and stems, small reddish-brown stipule projections at nodes, and green hairy cyathial cups edged by toothed white gland appendages. FNA describes HAIRY CAPSULES and pale 4-angled lightly wrinkled mature seeds, but the currently licensed macro set proves hairy cyathial cups NOT independently a mature hairy capsule or a loose seed. Contrast with low rounded-leaved glabrous E. fendleri. Formal BONAP/NAPA county nativity decision stays on HOLD.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. In E. angusta, the combination of erect perennial habit, very narrow distal leaves, uniform strigose pubescence, and hairy fruit is unusually distinctive.

key_traits.label: Growth form
key_traits.text: Perennial with moderately to strongly thickened rootstock; stems erect, about 12–43 cm.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite. Proximal blades ovate to ovate-elliptic; distal blades linear to elliptic-linear, about 7–41 × 2–5 mm and more than 6× as long as wide. Base asymmetric, cuneate to rounded; margins entire; apex acute; surfaces usually short-strigose.

key_traits.label: Stipules
key_traits.text: Distinct, linear-subulate or reduced to nodiform/papilliform structures, often reddish brown, about 0.1–0.7 mm, strigose.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: Solitary at distal nodes. Involucre strigose; 4 narrow oblong green to yellow-green glands with relatively showy white flabellate appendages whose distal margins are shallowly and irregularly toothed.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 2–2.6 × 2.5–3 mm, strigose.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds white, ovoid, 4-angled in cross section, about 1.7–2.2 × 1.1–1.2 mm, transversely low-ridged or wrinkled.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: distal leaves linear to elliptic-linear and more than 6× as long as wide

lookalikes.differences: Against E. fendleri, E. angusta is much taller and erect, with very narrow distal leaves and a hairy capsule; E. fendleri is a low clustered perennial with rounded entire glabrous leaves and glabrous capsule. Against the prostrate sandmats, the erect narrow-leaved silhouette is the quickest first split.
